title: How much more does a six year old sleep?
description: A smooth line graph of typical sleep by age is read at age six and between ages thirty and fifty. The video takes the two readings apart and breaks Keeko's doubt that the later reading of eight and a half hours belongs to ages thirty to fifty.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the line at the right age, then take away. Watch for students who read the wrong part of the curve.

source: About how much more sleep does a 6 year old get than a perso
video_script.why: The child has read single points on line graphs and now reads two ages on one smooth curve and compares them.
video_script.substitution: Find each age on the bottom axis, read the sleep on the side scale, and take the smaller reading from the larger.
video_script.anchor: the book's smooth line graph of the typical sleep duration of Indians across ages 6 to 75
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the right-hand part of the curve, about eight and a half hours, for the ages thirty to fifty.
video_script.payoff_line: a six year old sleeps about one and a half hours more a day

final_answer.spoken: a six year old sleeps about one and a half hours more a day

maths_rules: the graph shows the typical sleep time for ages 6 to 75 as a smooth curve
at age 6 the graph reads about 9.5 hours
the sleep time falls through the teenage years and touches about 8 hours between ages 30 and 50
after age 50 the sleep time rises again, reaching about 8.5 hours
slip: read the curve at the right age, not at its other end
video_script.design: One idea: read the curve at two ages and take the smaller from the larger. The wrong idea is reading the wrong part of the curve. The smooth curve stays on screen all video.
